gg3.same_expectation_why: It is the same bubble in the same corner, but it keeps changing - dark, pale grey, or with a tick - and I cannot tell if those are different jobs or one switch showing its state.
gg3.affects_navigation: Yes - if the same corner button sometimes starts a new chat and sometimes flips a hidden mode, I would stop trusting it and just avoid it.

first_pass.why: Same spot, same shape, but three different looks and no word anywhere, so I have to press it to find out what it does, and then I have to work out whether I changed something.
first_pass.solution: Put a short word next to it, like Temporary, and make the tick version obviously look switched on - and never grey it out without saying why.

test_cases.what_to_try: On the empty new chat, press the speech-bubble button at the top right once and look at what changed on the screen. Press it again and look again. Then press 'Create an image or sticker' and press the same button while it looks grey. Finish with the button back in its first look.
test_cases.real_if: after pressing each look you still cannot tell what it did, what state you are in, or whether the grey one does anything
test_cases.not_real_if: after pressing, the screen tells you plainly what each look means, and you could tell the plain, ticked and grey looks apart as one switch
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the dashed bubble once. The button got a tick, the middle of the empty page said 'Temporary chat - This chat won't appear in history', and the typing box said Temporary chat too. So the tick means temporary chat is on, and the screen says it in words. I pressed it again. The words flickered and then went away, and the button went back to dashed, so it is one on/off switch. Then I opened Create an image or sticker. The bubble turned pale grey, and when I pressed it a dark tip popped up saying this model does not support temporary chat. So the grey one tells me why it's grey, but only after I press it. That tip then got stuck on screen. Tapping it, Back and pressing the bubble again did nothing, and it only went away when I pressed a picture tile underneath. I closed the picture panel with its X and the bubble was back to its first dashed look. I finished.

test_cases.what_to_try: Press 'Create an image or sticker', then press the 'Sketch' picture so the drawing panel opens. With the drawing panel open, press the X at the top right beside Trending / Templates and see what closes. Then press 'Sketch' again and press the X at the left of the drawing tools and see what closes.
test_cases.real_if: one of the two X's closes something you did not expect, or you could not tell before pressing which one closes what
test_cases.not_real_if: each X closed what you expected it to close
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the picture panel and pressed Sketch. The white drawing panel came up with its own X on the left, and the other X was still showing at the top right. I expected the top X to close the whole picture panel. It didn't: it only closed the drawing panel and left the picture panel open. I opened Sketch again and pressed the X on the left of the drawing tools, and that also just closed the drawing panel. So the two X's did the same thing, but the top one did not do what I expected, and I could not have told that before pressing. I needed a third press on the top X to actually close the picture panel. I finished, but only by pressing X's until the screen looked right.

gg7.same_expectation_why: They all say the same two words, so maybe they do the same, but if they are old chats they must each open something different and nothing tells me which.
gg7.affects_navigation: Yes - I would open the wrong one, then another, then another, and by then I have forgotten what I was looking for.

first_pass.why: Four identical rows saying Create image in one list, no dates, no heading telling me these are my past chats - I cannot find my own work without opening every one.
first_pass.solution: A heading like Recent chats above that list, and a date or the first few words of each chat so the rows are not all the same.

test_cases.what_to_try: Open the side menu with the two-line button at the top left. In the list of chats, find two rows with the same words (for example the two 'Greeting exchange' rows). Before pressing, say which one you think is which. Press the first, look, open the menu again and press the second.
test_cases.real_if: you could not tell the two rows apart before pressing, or one opened something you did not expect
test_cases.not_real_if: you could tell them apart, or what opened matched what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: In the side menu there were two rows both saying 'Greeting exchange', plus 'Create red apple image' and 'Create Red Apple Image' next to each other. Before pressing, I honestly could not tell the two Greeting rows apart. My only guess was that the top one is newer. The first one opened a chat where I said Hello and it answered 'How can I help you today?'. The chat has no title at the top, so I still didn't know which one I was in. When I opened the menu again, that row was lightly shaded, which helped a bit. The second one opened a different chat: Hello, 'How can I help you tonight?', then Thanks and 'You're very welcome!'. So they really are different chats with the same name, and nothing in the list tells them apart until you open them.

test_cases.what_to_try: Open the side menu and open any past chat from the list. Open the side menu again and press the big 'ChatGPT' at the top of it; note where you land. Open a past chat again and press the pencil-in-a-square at the top right; note where you land. Open a past chat again, open the side menu and press the blue 'Chat' button; note where you land.
test_cases.real_if: one of the three took you somewhere you did not expect, or you could not have told beforehand that they do the same thing
test_cases.not_real_if: each of the three did what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: From a past Greeting chat, I opened the menu and pressed the big word ChatGPT at the top. I expected nothing, since it looks like a heading, but it took me to a fresh empty chat. Then I opened Hello Greeting and pressed the pencil-in-a-square at the top right, and got a fresh empty chat, as I expected. Then I opened Greeting Response, opened the menu and pressed the blue Chat button, and got a fresh empty chat again, as expected. So all three do the same thing, but I could not have known the heading does it. The pencil and the Chat button share a picture; the heading gives no hint.

test_cases.what_to_try: Press '+' at the left of the typing bar, press 'Photos', look, and come back with the phone's Back button without choosing anything. Then press 'Create an image or sticker', press the 'Stickers' picture, and in the sentence press the word 'Photo'; look at what appears. Press 'Choose photo' if offered, look, and come back without choosing anything. Close the sticker page with the X at the top left.
test_cases.real_if: before pressing it you would not have known the 'Photo' word in the sentence leads to choosing a photo like 'Photos' does
test_cases.not_real_if: you would have known, or the two led you to the same kind of place as you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed + and then Photos. The phone's photo picker slid up, empty ('No photos yet'), and I backed out with Back without choosing anything. Then I opened Create an image or sticker and pressed Stickers, and the page with the sentence 'Create a 3D sticker pack based on Photo, remixing with...' came up. Before pressing, I thought Photo was a word I could swap. When I pressed it, a small menu popped up with Take photo and Choose photo. I pressed Choose photo and got the very same photo picker as before. I backed out without choosing, then closed the sticker page with the X at the top left. So before pressing I would not have known the Photo word leads there. But one press shows two plain choices and lands in the same picker, so I'd know next time. I finished.
